transcript:
Live from NPR News in Washington, I'm Rylan Barton.
Ukraine's president is urging world leaders to help end what he calls Russia's "crazy
war" against his country.
The U.S. and European countries are worried that the conflict is spreading, as NPR's Michelle
Kellerman reports.
Ukrainian President Vladimir Zelensky says it's madness that Russia keeps fighting to
try to take Ukrainian land, even as Ukrainian drones and missiles damage Russia's energy
sector.
Russia offered a cease-fire if Russia stops bombing civilian infrastructure and blocking
grain shipments.
Secretary of State Marco Rubio came out of talks with Russia's foreign minister, saying
both sides are interested in limited steps on grain and energy.
"It doesn't solve the war, but it does, I think, in some ways potentially alleviate
some of the global pressures that are being felt as a result of that."
But Europeans say Russia is expanding the conflict and threatening NATO airspace.
The U.S. Ambassador Mike Waltz calls that unacceptable.
Michelle Kellerman, NPR News, New York.
Staff at Camp Mystic in Kerr County, Texas, are being investigated for manslaughter and
other criminal offenses.
Twenty-eight people died at the girls' summer camp in July 2025 during flooding in the state's
Hill country.
Kaylee Hunt from member station KUT reports.
Court records show Texas Rangers executed 14 search warrants against the owners of Camp
Mystic and several of their staff members.
The warrants, which were executed last week, allow the Rangers to investigate their personal
electronic data from the deadly flooding event last year.
The documents show Rangers believed the camp may have committed multiple criminal offenses,
including manslaughter, criminally negligent homicide, and injury to a child, by failing
to fulfill its operator's duty to prepare for, monitor, and actively respond to recognize
hazards during the flooding.
It's not clear when or if a case against the camp will be presented to a Kerr County
grand jury.
For NPR News, I'm Kaylee Hunt in Austin.
President Trump says he supports a temporary ban on U.S. diesel exports as prices hover
at record highs.
NPR's Windsor Johnston reports diesels averaging about $6.50 a gallon nationwide.
Even drivers who never put diesel in their own tanks could still end up paying more at
the checkout line.
When businesses pay more to move goods, some of that expense gets passed along to consumers.
Mark Wolf is with the National Energy Assistance Directors Association.
The diesel fuel is essential for trucks, for deliveries, and I think that those prices
are being passed on as we speak, and so grocery costs are going up because groceries have
to be delivered by trucks.
Wolf says perishable foods could be among the first places consumers notice the difference
because they're delivered daily.
The Trump administration is now weighing a full or partial ban on diesel exports, but
some energy officials warned that could push prices higher in parts of the country.
Windsor Johnston, NPR News.
Major U.S. stock indexes sank today.
This is NPR News.
The World Health Organization warns that Congo is running short of health workers to staff
treatment centers for the fastest-growing Ebola outbreak in history.
The outbreak has spread to seven provinces with more than 7,700 confirmed cases and 3,700
deaths.
The outbreak remains uncontrolled.
Suicide was the 10th leading cause of death in the U.S. in 2024, according to the CDC.
As NPR's Ritu Chatterjee reports, the suicide rate went down slightly for several groups
compared to the year before.
More than 48,000 people died by suicide across the country in 2024.
That's nearly 500 fewer deaths than in 2023.
The New Report finds that the rate of suicide deaths fell for women aged 25 and above.
Women aged 65 to 74 years saw the biggest drop in suicide rate, an 11.3 percent decline
in 2024 compared to the year prior.
The suicide rate also dropped slightly among males, but only for those between the ages
of 15 and 44.
The overall suicide rate among men has remained three to four times higher than for women
in the past decade.
Firearms remained the leading cause of suicides in both men and women in 2024, and the rates
remained unchanged compared to the year before.
Ritu Chatterjee, NPR News.
The Oxford English Dictionary has officially added over a dozen Caribbean words.
Bimpert, a Bermudian term for a foolish person, is included.
Horner Mann from Trinidad and Tobago describes an unfaithful man.
The dictionary now holds over 500,000 words and phrases.
This is NPR News from Washington.
